To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

extraneous news reduces the immediate stock price reaction to earnings news, increases the drift in stock prices after earnings news, and increases the profitability of trading strategies that exploit this drift.

the arrival of a lot of competing information on the same day causes a firm’s stock price to react more sluggishly to its earnings surprise, causes the firm’s post-earnings drift to be stronger, and causes the profitability of a trading strategy that exploits drift to be greater.

the arrival of competing news reduces the magnitude of the immediate stock price reaction to a firm's earnings news, but it increases the magnitude of the post-earnings-announcement drift in stock returns.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of attention on investor behavior.
a phenomenon of investor behavior that is both interesting and important.
the question of how much attention investors pay to a given earnings announcement and how that attention is affected by other events occurring at the same time as the announcement.
